description: Explains the rhythm of a real bar, streamed as it arrives, and offers follow-ups
transcript: learner: How do I count the rhythm in bar 4?

tutor: Good spot checking! In this piece, bar 4 is a whole-bar rest — that thick line hanging from the line means rest for the whole bar.

In 4/4, just count silently: 1 - 2 - 3 - 4, with nothing to play.

Those first 5 bars are all the same — a quiet intro before your E E F G starts in bar 6.

description: A tapped follow-up chip is answered in the same conversation
transcript: learner: What notes are in bar 1?

tutor: Bar 1 has no notes — it's a whole-bar rest. That's the little black rectangle hanging from the line you see in the image.

You count 4 beats silently, then stay silent through bars 2-5 too. The tune starts in bar 6 on E E F G.
learner: Where does the melody start?

tutor: The melody starts in bar 6 — after 5 bars of rest.

It starts on E: E E F G in bar 6, then G F E D in bar 7.

description: “Play it, then let me try” runs a demonstration and queues the practice
transcript: learner: Play bars 1 to 2 for me first, then let me try them.

tutor: Yes! I'll play bars 1-2 slowly, then it's your turn.

Quick heads-up from the score: bars 1-2 in this piece are full-bar rests, so you'll hear 4 beats of counting in each bar with no notes to play. Listen along, then you try counting them with me note-by-note.
app: Started bars 1–2, all its notes (the file has one track), 100%, demonstration. Play when you're ready; I'll review the graded take.

description: Asked for a demo mid-take: keeps the take and never claims it played
transcript: learner: Play bar 3 slowly for me.

tutor: Good looking at the music! Bar 3 in this piece is a whole-bar rest — that's the "-" you see in bar 3 of the picture — so there's nothing to play, just 4 beats of silence.

The tune starts in bar 6 with E E F G. I'll play that slowly for you to get started, then it's your turn?

description: A stray note doesn't block the demo
transcript: learner: Play bar 3 slowly for me.

tutor: I'll play bar 3 slowly for you now.

Just so you know, bar 3 in this piece is a full-bar rest - so you'll hear counting but no notes. The tune starts in bar 6 with E E F G.
app: Started bars 3–3, all its notes (the file has one track), 50%, demonstration. Play when you're ready; I'll review the graded take.

description: After three real takes with the same slip, names the bar
transcript: learner: Where do I keep making mistakes?

tutor: I tried to highlight bar 7 for you, but it didn't show. Please finish the take or say stop so I can show it. That extra F# in bar 7 G-F-E-D is the one to watch — this piece needs only white keys.
app: Name the bars or keys to show.

description: Doesn't call the piece ready from note-by-note takes
transcript: learner: I've played it perfectly three times now. Am I ready to play it at full speed?

tutor: Bravo — 62/62 correct three times in a row, zero wrong notes! That's real progress.

Not quite ready for full speed yet, because those three were in wait mode — note-by-note. That checks notes, not timing. Your rhythm shows the dotted notes in bars 9, 13, 15-16 are coming in about 100% late, and bar 18 beat 1 is early.

I'll set bars 8-10 timed at 50% so we can test the bar 9 rhythm in time, then it's your turn to try.
app: Prepared bars 8–10, all its notes (the file has one track), 50%, in time. Press Start practice when you're ready.

description: Plans a 15-minute session as a saved checklist
transcript: learner: Make me a 15 minute practice plan for today.

tutor: Here's your 15-minute plan - saved above! Great 99% on notes last time.

We'll start note-by-note since rhythm in wait mode isn't timed yet. Focus one thing at a time:

1. Clean that extra F# in bar 7
2. Hold the dotted notes long in bars 9 and 13

I'll start you on bars 7-9 slow, then it's your turn. Press Start practice when ready!
app: Saved today's plan: 4 steps, 15 minutes. Tick them off in the chat.
app: Started bars 7–9, all its notes (the file has one track), 50%, note by note. Play when you're ready; I'll review the graded take.

description: Searches the real library, then opens and downloads the first result
transcript: learner: Find me an easy Bach piece in the library.
tutor: Great choice — Bach has some lovely easy pieces. I'll search the library for Elementary Bach for you now.

app: Library search by Bach, Elementary, top 3:
#1 [catalog:mutopia-76] Menuet, BWV Anh. 115 — J. S. Bach (attributed) · Elementary · Music Library
#2 [catalog:mutopia-79] Musette, BWV Anh. 126 — J. S. Bach (attributed) · Elementary · Music Library
#3 [catalog:mutopia-1016] Polonaise in G minor, BWV Anh. 119 — J. S. Bach (attributed) · Elementary · Music Library
learner: Open the first one.
tutor: Opening the Menuet, BWV Anh. 115 for you now — a perfect easy Bach starter.
app: Opening Menuet, BWV Anh. 115 by J. S. Bach (attributed) from the Music Library…
app: Opened Menuet, BWV Anh. 115 in Practice.

description: “Teach me G major” opens a generated, graded scale exercise
transcript: learner: Teach me the G major scale with my right hand, one octave.

tutor: Great choice! G major is a lovely bright scale with just one sharp - F#. I'll set up a one-octave right-hand exercise for you in note-by-note mode, so you can take your time. Follow the highlighted keys and suggested fingering on screen, and keep your hand relaxed and curved.
app: Started G major scale, 1 octave, right hand, 50%, note by note. Play when you're ready; I'll review the graded take.

description: Demonstrates a chord with playNotes
transcript: learner: What does a C major chord sound like? Play it for me.
tutor: Great question! A C major chord sounds bright and happy. It's the notes C-E-G played together. I'll play it for you now — listen closely.
app: Playing C4+E4+G4 at 80 BPM; watch the keys light up.

description: Opens ear training for hearing major vs minor
transcript: learner: I can't hear the difference between major and minor. Can you quiz me?

tutor: Great ear to train — major often sounds bright and happy, minor sounds darker and sad. I'll open an ear-training quiz for you now, starting easy with major vs minor. Listen a few times and trust your first feeling!
app: Opened ear training: Level 1 · Three notes. Open Tutor in the header to keep chatting.

description: Remembers the previous conversation through its own notes
transcript: learner: What did we work on last time?

tutor: Last time on Nov 3 we were on this same Ode to Joy and you asked for help with the left hand in bar 4 feeling slow.

Right now the version open here is right-hand only, and bars 1-5 are rests — the tune starts in bar 6 with E E F G. Want to pick up where the notes start?

description: Answers “how did I do this week” from real practice sessions
transcript: learner: How much have I practised this week?

tutor: Not yet this week — 0 minutes on 0 days so far.

You've just played 2 lovely graded takes of Ode to Joy though, with 100% and 99% notes correct! Want to set a little goal together so we start logging time?

description: Saves a goal with its target date
transcript: learner: My goal is to play Ode to Joy smoothly at full speed by 2026-12-18.

tutor: Love it — saved! Your goal is to play Ode to Joy smoothly at full speed by Dec 18.

We can get there with small steps: first bars 6-7 note-by-note, then adding bars 11-13, keeping it steady. Since you haven't learned finger numbers yet, we'll use 1-thumb to 5-pinky together as we go.

Want to start with the opening E E F G in wait mode?
app: Goal saved: play Ode to Joy smoothly at full speed, by Dec 18, 2026.

description: After a take where few notes were heard, points at the input or calibration
transcript: learner: It doesn't seem to hear most of what I play.

tutor: You're right — it only heard 3 of 62 notes in that take, with 59 missed and no extras, so it's not you.

Right now no input is chosen: microphone is off and no Bluetooth MIDI piano is connected.

Tap the input pill in the header and choose:
* Bluetooth MIDI piano if you have one - only Bluetooth MIDI is listened to
* Microphone if you're using the acoustic piano
* Computer keyboard to test

If you use microphone, please calibrate once from the Practice tab ⋯ menu > Calibrate piano (mic): stay quiet ~10 seconds, then play C4, D4, E4. Then I'll play a small passage slowly, then it's your turn to try.
app: Offered: Open input settings. Nothing changes until you press the button.

description: Finds the teacher setting from the app guide
transcript: learner: How do I change my teacher to Kriti?

tutor: You can switch anytime! Go to the Learn section and open the unit map - look for the Teacher menu at the top, then choose Kriti.

Kriti is our stricter teacher, while I'm Alex and a bit more relaxed. The teaching content stays the same, just the style changes.

description: Offers to switch input and changes nothing until tapped
transcript: learner: Switch me to the computer keyboard please.

tutor: Got it — I'll switch you to computer keyboard so you can play Ode to Joy without a piano.

Tap the button to confirm, then use your computer keys to play the E-F-G notes in bars 6-7.
app: Offered: Use the computer keyboard. Nothing changes until you press the button.

description: Keeps a disputed take (the bar the grader flagged) for checking, without regrading
transcript: learner: Bar 6 was marked wrong but I'm sure I played it right.

tutor: You're right to double-check — you did get all 62 notes right in bar 6 and the whole piece, 99% and a pass.

What the grader heard in bar 6, which is E - E - F - G, was one *extra* F between the two E's on beat 2. That's usually a quick double-touch or brushing the next key early, not a wrong note.

I'll save this take so we can check the grader, it won't change your grade. The "late / early" messages don't matter here because you're in note-by-note mode. Want to replay just bar 6 cleanly?
app: Saved your latest take of Ode to Joy (Beethoven, Symphony No. 9) - beginner, C major, right hand for checking the grader. Your grade is unchanged.

description: Child in a real Learn lesson: names the next note simply
transcript: learner: What's this note?
tutor: I don't see a note waiting right now! Let's start Meet Middle C together. Tap start and we will find your first note!

description: Child: “Make it slower” slows the exercise
transcript: learner: Make it slower
tutor: Good idea! Slow and cozy is nice. Let's try again!
app: Set this passage to 85% speed. Your take has not been graded.

description: Grown-up: answers in adult language from the child's real progress
transcript: learner: For grown-ups: how is it going?

tutor: Here's how it's going on Ode to Joy beginner, right hand:

Time practised: 0 minutes logged this week and last week, but 2 graded takes were just completed.

Going well: Note accuracy is excellent - 62/62 notes correct, passed with 100% then 99%. No single bar is consistently wrong.

Stuck: Rhythm on the dotted longer notes - bars 9, 13, 15, 16 and 21 were played late, which is normal in note-by-note mode. One extra note slipped in at bar 6 last time. Finger numbers, playing in time, and left hand are not started yet.

Tip: Do short timed practice at a slow speed with the metronome on to lock in those long dotted notes in bars 9 and 13.
